key.mechanism: the operator's own ssh: the agent, `~/.ssh/config` and the default identities
key.prompt: none — `BatchMode=yes` makes a key-less account fail loudly instead of hanging a GUI

password.mechanism: OpenSSH `SSH_ASKPASS`, forced; the helper prints the password it reads from its environment

askpass.program: prints the variable to stdout as UTF-8, exactly one line
askpass.windowsNote: the Windows client runs a `.cmd` helper; a spaced path was measured working

password.forgottenWhen: the far side answers `Permission denied` or `Auth fail`
password.libraryRequirement: a client without ssh must answer keyboard-interactive as well as password; setting a password covers only one of the two

hostKeys.unknownHost: trusted on first use, and remembered in the operator's own known_hosts
hostKeys.changedHost: **refused** — the connection fails and nothing is sent to the host
hostKeys.changedHostRecovery: the operator removes the stale entry from known_hosts themselves; nothing in this application rewrites or bypasses it
hostKeys.libraryWarning: JSch: `no` also accepts a changed key; true accept-new needs a custom HostKeyRepository with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes

teardown.by: close the remote command's stdin, and let the far side reap itself

staleLaunch.identityCheck: a pid is killed only while it is still a powershell.exe running -EncodedCommand, or a node.exe carrying this launcher's argv
staleLaunch.cleanedBy: the launch that wrote it, in its own teardown
staleLaunch.posix: not recorded: the POSIX branch reads stdin through `cat > /dev/null` and was measured to reap on disconnect, and a Windows-only gap must not change the other branch
staleLaunch.why: two Harnesses over one DSH home cannot share Session write leases, so "one" and "none" are the only useful states

directoryRule.posix: split `~` off `~` and `~/...`, quote only the remainder: cd "$HOME"/'work/dsh'
directoryRule.windows: `~` and `~\` are joined onto $env:USERPROFILE, then Set-Location -LiteralPath

directorySafety.agreement: both clients refuse the same characters, so a device book is portable between them
directorySafety.whyHere: the reference client cannot escape a directory into the single command string it hands to cmd.exe, and `%`/`!` expand even inside double quotes
directorySafety.whyStill: the Android client has no shell in the path and does not need the restriction; it applies it to stay interoperable

record.permissions: POSIX `chmod 600`; Windows inherits the DSH home ACL

output.adopted: HOST adopted pid=<n> port=<n> token=<t> started=<iso>
output.started: HOST started pid=<n> port=<n> token=<t> started=<iso>
output.readiness: dsh web: <url> — the existing readiness line, printed after the HOST line

identity.not: a timestamp is not evidence, and neither is the record alone

lock.release: the ensure program removes it, including on failure (`trap … EXIT` / `finally`)

launch.posix: `nohup dsh web --no-open --port 0 </dev/null >>log 2>&1 &` — `nohup` execs, so `$!` is the Harness pid
launch.posixWhy: `setsid` forks when its caller leads a process group, so the pid it leaves is not reliably the Harness
launch.windows: a generated `.cmd` created by `Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process Create`
launch.windowsWhy: the created process has a `WmiPrvSE.exe` parent, so the ssh session has no handle to it; a `Start-Process` inside the session does
launch.windowsQuoting: a `.cmd` file, because `cmd /c ""set "X=…" && …""` is parsed wrong and reports `'"set "PROBE_INLINE' is not recognized`
